A1.justification: Both complete, 17-page PDFs describe the same ORT research. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the equations, figures, tables, and appendices, including content retained under different appendix letters.

before.justification: V1 reports original ORT evaluations on WebQSP and CWQ, comparisons across three LLMs, ablations, and detailed results in Tables 1–4 and 6.

after.justification: V2 retains the original WebQSP and CWQ experiments, model comparisons, ablations, and appendix results.

M1.justification: The recognition, reverse ontology traversal, pruning, and guided answer-mining procedures remain unchanged, as do Algorithm 1 and the prompts. V2 clarifies aim entities and documents implementation details without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same English Freebase KGQA coverage using WebQSP and CWQ. The added references to medical and scientific applications do not introduce evaluated domains or tasks.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain identical baseline membership in Tables 1–3 and 6, including the same embedding, retrieval, fine-tuned KGQA, standalone LLM, MindMap, and KG Retriever methods.

E3.justification: The test sets, graph statistics, metrics, and evaluated model configurations are unchanged, including 1,628 WebQSP and 3,531 CWQ questions. Appendix B first discloses numerical traversal limits; neither version establishes a revision to the existing experiments.

E4.justification: Table 4 retains the same w/o LLM Filter, Trace Forward, and w/o Rules ablations. Tables 7–8 retain the Lou Seal and Ovadia Yosef case studies with identical paths and answers.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without run or seed counts, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests. No statistical reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: All eight tables retain identical content, and Figures 5–6 retain their values. For example, Table 1 still reports ORT Hit@1/F1 of 89.4/71.8 on WebQSP and 72.9/62.6 on CWQ.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations 1–6, and pruning pseudocode are unchanged. The added implementation explanations introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims remain ontology-guided reverse reasoning, plug-and-play LLM enhancement, and state-of-the-art performance on the studied benchmarks. The shortened abstract retains the same proposed solution and performance claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations of benchmark results and ablation tradeoffs remain unchanged, as do both limitations concerning irrelevant entities and paths. The expanded aim-entity discussion clarifies the existing label-mapping mechanism without changing its scientific interpretation.

D1.justification: New Appendix B explains extracting entity labels from relation names and constructing ontology triples. It also specifies MAX_POP = 5 and TOP_K = 10, where v1 provided symbolic limits without numerical settings. These are useful additional reproducibility details.

R1.justification: The introduction adds citations to Li et al. (2025), SparkRA, and Medical Graph RAG, including replacing the sentiment-analysis citation to Devlin et al. The KGQA positioning in Section 4 remains unchanged; the shortened DeepSeek reference describes the same work.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized abstract and introduction edits, expands explanations in Sections 2.1 and 2.2.2, adds implementation and acknowledgement sections, and updates affiliation/contact details. Existing appendix content is retained under shifted letters, with the overall narrative preserved.

P2.justification: Existing displays reflow: Table 1 moves from PDF page 5 to 6, Figure 6 from page 6 to 7, and Algorithm 1 changes position within page 4. Case-table spacing also changes, while figure content, axes, legends, and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves reproducibility by explaining label and ontology construction and supplying previously unstated traversal limits in Appendix B. Section 2.1 also clarifies the intermediate role of aim entities. These additions resolve specific documentation gaps, while the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged, making the overall improvement limited.
